summary: Three people were arrested in the Fairbanks area overnight — two near Nenana and one in Fairbanks — and no court case had been opened in any of the three by early Friday. A Fairbanks grand jury indicted a woman on a Class A felony drug charge on Oct. 29. The robbery charge filed after an Oct. 12 incident at a Fairbanks sporting goods store was amended on Oct. 16 to a misdemeanor theft charge; a correction appears below. The Alaska Court System's weekly report of charges filed, covering Oct. 23 to Oct. 29, lists 48 cases at the four courthouses in the area — but 11 case numbers the Fairbanks court opened on Oct. 28 are absent from it for the second week running, so the report's count is lower than the number of cases actually opened in its own window. The court's companion report of cases closed has not been updated since Oct. 26.

entries.title: Warrant arrest: Michael Latham
body: Michael Latham, 56, of Willow, was arrested on an outstanding warrant for a parole violation and on charges of driving while his license was revoked and having no motor vehicle liability insurance. Mile 320 of the Parks Highway near Nenana, Oct. 29 at 8:36 p.m.; Alaska State Troopers.

Driving while license revoked means operating a vehicle after the state has withdrawn the driving privilege. Troopers say they stopped a 2001 Dodge pickup for several moving and equipment violations, including almost driving off the road in a construction zone, and found the driver had an outstanding warrant.
He was remanded to the Fairbanks Correctional Center. No court case had been opened in the matter as of early Oct. 30.

entries.title: Assault arrest: Emily Vance
body: Emily Vance, 40, of Nenana, was arrested on charges of assault in the fourth degree and criminal mischief in the fifth degree. Near 2nd Street, Nenana, Oct. 29 at about 5:18 p.m.; Alaska State Troopers.

Assault in the fourth degree covers injuring another person or placing them in fear of injury; criminal mischief in the fifth degree covers damaging property worth less than $250. Troopers say she entered a residence, caused damage to the front door and assaulted a person there.
She was taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center and held without bail. No court case had been opened in the matter as of early Oct. 30.

entries.title: Assault arrest: Maya Jade Newman
body: Maya Jade Newman, 25, was arrested on charges of assault in the fourth degree — causing fear of imminent injury — and unlawful contact, both recorded by police as misdemeanors. 1500 block of Denali Way, Fairbanks, Oct. 29 at 5:32 p.m.; Fairbanks Police.
Assault in the fourth degree in this form covers placing another person in fear of immediate injury. Police case 26003311.
No court case had been opened in the matter as of early Oct. 30.

entries.title: Drug indictment: Rayann Marlisa Carroll
body: Rayann Marlisa Carroll has been indicted on a charge of misconduct involving a controlled substance in the second degree — making or delivering a schedule IA controlled substance — a Class A felony, punishable by up to 20 years.

A Fairbanks grand jury returned the indictment on Oct. 29 and the case was transferred to the Superior Court the same day. The charge was first filed on Oct. 21 and the offense is recorded as having taken place at Fairbanks on Oct. 20.

Case 4FA-26-02128CR; superior court arraignment Nov. 4 before Judge Thomas Temple, with an omnibus hearing Dec. 17 and a trial week beginning Jan. 4, 2027. An indictment is a grand jury's finding that a case may go forward and is not a conviction.

entries.title: Robbery charge amended to misdemeanor theft: Daniel Zachary Schwietert
body: The charge against Daniel Zachary Schwietert, arising from an Oct. 12 incident at a Fairbanks sporting goods store, is now attempted theft in the third degree — taking property worth $250 to $749 — a Class B misdemeanor. The court file records an original charge of robbery in the first degree, a Class A felony, and an amended charge entered on Oct. 16.
Troopers said at the time that they were called to Beaver Sports in Fairbanks at 1:46 p.m. on Oct. 12 for a reported robbery and arrested him.
Case 4FA-26-02078CR; a change of plea hearing was set for Oct. 30 before Judge Ben Seekins. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Criminal mischief charge: Dalton Curtis Wayne Benefield
body: Dalton Curtis Wayne Benefield is charged with criminal mischief in the fourth degree — damaging property worth $250 to $749 — a Class A misdemeanor, recorded in the court file as domestic violence related.

Troopers say they responded to a disturbance on Homer Drive in North Pole on Oct. 28, found extensive damage to the residence they attribute to Benefield, estimated the damage at more than $750, and arrested him on a charge of criminal mischief in the third degree. The charge filed in court is one degree lower.
Case 4FA-26-02178CR; pre-trial conference Dec. 24 and a trial week beginning Jan. 4, 2027.

entries.title: Driving with a suspended license: James Patrick Carpentino
body: James Patrick Carpentino, 48, of North Pole, is charged with driving with a license in violation of limits with a previous conviction, a Class A misdemeanor. The charge was entered on the court file on Oct. 29.

Troopers say they stopped him at about 5:09 p.m. on Oct. 27 for a moving violation and found he was driving while his license was suspended for a criminal offense, with a prior conviction for the same offense in the past 10 years. He was taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center.
Case 4FA-26-02176CR; arraignment Nov. 3.

entries.title: Court's weekly list of closed cases has not been updated since Oct. 26
body: The Alaska Court System's weekly report of criminal cases disposed, which lists cases closed statewide, still carries the data of Oct. 26 and has not been refreshed on any of the four mornings since.
No Interior case closed after Oct. 26 can be read from it. The court's companion report of criminal charges filed has been refreshed each morning over the same period, most recently on Oct. 30.
